input.summary:
Implemented a full Task Management REST API in TypeScript using only Node.js built-in modules. Here's what was built:

## File Structure
- **`src/types.ts`** — All TypeScript interfaces and types (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification, HTTP helpers, status transitions)
- **`src/store.ts`** — In-memory data store using Maps, with ID generation (crypto.randomUUID) and notification factory
- **`src/helpers.ts`** — HTTP response builders (ok/created/noContent/badRequest/notFound/conflict/unprocessable) and validation utilities
- **`src/router.ts`** — Pattern-based URL router with dynamic `:param` segment matching and method dispatch
- **`src/server.ts`** — HTTP server with async body reading, JSON parsing, URL/query parsing, and error handling
- **`src/handlers/users.ts`** — CRUD for users with unique-email enforcement
- **`src/handlers/projects.ts`** — CRUD for projects + member add/remove with duplicate detection
- **`src/handlers/tasks.ts`** — CRUD for tasks + status transitions (todo→in-progress→done) + assignment; notifications fired on assign and status change
- **`src/handlers/comments.ts`** — CRUD for comments with task/author validation; notifications sent to assignee and project members on comment creation
- **`src/handlers/notifications.ts`** — List (filterable by userId) + mark-as-read
- **`src/main.ts`** — Entry point, starts server on PORT (default 3000)
- **`src/demo.ts`** — End-to-end demo that starts the server on a random port and exercises all features with ✓/✗ assertions

## Key Features
- Enforced status transitions with 422 Unprocessable responses for invalid jumps
- Notifications automatically generated for task assignment, status changes, and comments
- Query string filtering for tasks (?projectId=), comments (?taskId=), notifications (?userId=)
- Full validation with appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 405, 409, 422)
- All 6 demo sections (Users, Projects, Tasks, Comments, Notifications, Cleanup) pass all assertions
